record_notes.DCP-LETT-2086: May 1, 1857; all nine body blocks, eleven notes and bibliography read. Home heading is deliberately not actual composition place: body locates writing at water cure, apparatus Moor Park. Thanks missing October 10, 1856 Wallace letter received only a few days earlier; no exact receipt day. Distinct 1855 Annals paper read and largely agreed with, not identical to missing personal letter. Domestic/natural variety separation, hybrid evidence and climatic effects qualified; definite idea not proof of truth. Poultry results disappointing, pigeon study fruitful; Brooke specimens received. Black-jaguar pairing explicitly needs evidence beyond offspring colour. Parrot diet versus induced feather colour distinct. Twenty-year research claim and two-year publication forecast are contemporary estimates, not dates of eventual publication.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2145: Supplied September 27, 1857 from Darwin endorsement plus explicit December 22 acknowledgment; both surviving body blocks, three notes, annotations and bibliography read. Opening, internal end and remaining pages missing. P1 responds to May praise of species paper and says detailed proof partly written and requires English resources. P2 answers May black-jaguar question but expressly not capable of proof; locality/skin-trade observations and form impression do not establish assortative mating. Darwin month annotation is not receipt date. Surviving disappointment passage is directly answered in 2192; land-shell, human and island-connection questions mentioned there are absent from this fragment.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2192: December 22, 1857; all seven blocks, twelve notes and bibliography read. Explicitly thanks September 27 letter; surviving 2145 disappointment passage supports P1 response about attention to Annals paper and speculative agreement. P2 explicitly has NOT yet seen Aru paper; later apparatus quotations cannot imply completed reading. P3 discussions of subsidence and continental connections, P4 shells, P5 man and P6 future travel refer to missing portions of incoming or other sources; do not synthesize. Coral-map decision, Lyell/Hooker discussions and mollusc trials are historical claims, not current prompt text. Blyth calling attention matches independently preserved 1792 P1; a later knowledge witness, not exact arrival or first reading. Half-written work/two-year forecast and three months on hybridism remain estimates; December 29 completion is future apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2850: After August 1856, incomplete and damaged incoming; all eight blocks, nine notes and separate annotations read, no bibliography section. XML August 2 lower bound conflicts with ordinary after-August wording and upper 1882 is indexing envelope: exact composition and period inclusion held. Emma illness suggests earlier than October 1857 only editorially, not exact date. Jacobin offspring and reciprocal finch/canary crossings distinguish own successes, failures and friend report; German book and June journal requests do not identify the missing later cover. Literal nec-essary and damage marks require supported rendering treatment. P7 addressee is heading, not future letter content. Undated portfolio 17 and crossing marks do not date receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2048F: February 7, supplied 1857; seven blocks, eight notes and bibliography read. Response to missing Brent legal-affairs letter and silk-cock offer, not October 23 incoming 2158. Silk cock declined because young and hen available; flight remains question. German pouter inquiry and conditional price/transport instructions do not prove purchase or delivery. Cottage Gardener request by itself does not identify 2850, whose fragment lacks legal/cock matters. Body says Tegetmeier letter this morning while apparatus cross-reference is February 6; retain tension rather than alter day. Book on Variation is then-current species project, not completed 1868 book.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2158: October 23, 1857 incomplete incoming; six blocks, four notes, all annotations and bibliography read. Explicit yesterday Darwin letter personally received this morning identifies missing October 22 query, not February 7 letter. Finch/canary eggs hatch well after pairing in own experience; hybrid females lay variably sized eggs but mice/different nesting problems prevent inference of progeny. Reared offspring from supplied eggs is not her biological offspring. Male-hybrid productivity alleged but not witnessed; fancier age rule attributed. P6 fragment ends mid-account. Undated Darwin Q marks and reciprocal note remain separate from Brent testimony; no exact Darwin receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1845F: March 25, supplied 1856, photocopy of four-page ALS. All five blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Proof sheets received this morning and 32 pages assessed; full book/proofs not preserved here. Cattle observations answered without surviving source wording; further breeding, dogs/sheep/poultry and beauty questions posed. Body historical claims about peoples are source attribution, not established modern facts. P5 beauty query uniquely answered by surviving 1850; missing cattle response cannot be recreated from later Variation quotation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1850: Supplied April 6, 1856 by Darwin endorsement presumed copied from missing page; all three fragment blocks, three notes, separate annotations and bibliography read. P1 answers 1845F P5 beauty query, with generalizations attributed to Andersson. P2 asks about puma and lion flesh; Darwin puma account referenced in apparatus is prior book, not fresh reply. P3 contains signature and addressee requiring separation at export. Annotation date supports proposed composition but not exact receipt; cattle response absent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2021: December 23, supplied 1856; four blocks, five notes and bibliography read. First personal approach requesting variability comparison across time/place with roughly equal sample sizes; variable attachment is a confound. Forbes and Woodward discussions not enough definite light. P1 presents competing indications, not a settled universal statement. No incoming prompt for this new query; 2024 directly answers.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2024: December 29, 1856; all five blocks, six notes and bibliography read. Explicitly received December 23 Darwin letter yesterday morning, December 28; this is Davidson receipt, not Darwin receipt of this reply. P1–2 address variability with grown individuals, intermediate forms, consistency across places and habitat-linked differences; inability to give decisive conclusion must accompany examples. P3 requests Cirripedia purchase information for Bouchard, not proof he has read it; future monograph plates planned. Later Natural selection citation not exact incoming arrival.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1816A: January 3, supplied 1856; three blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Farnborough heading anomalous after address change but apparatus dates by publication circumstances, not automatic redating. Missing recent Davy note says experiments continuing; January 10 continuation cannot be its prompt. Earlier paper delayed in publication, royal council discussion and future publication distinct from March 1855 receipt/reading. Two epistolary papers and later journals must not be merged; no incoming authentic prompt currently survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1819A: January 10, 1856 catalogue record; full single bracketed editorial synopsis, one footnote and bibliography inspected. Authentic epistolary body unavailable in this preserved page. Synopsis describes ova experiments and age-dependent resistance; those third-person sentences are not Davy words or exportable prompt. Intended Royal Society communication differs from dispatch, public reading and publication. It postdates January 3 outgoing; candidate published-text recovery is separate and does not yet change admission.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1634: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. January 30, 1855 incoming Davy letter. Received missing Darwin enquiry this morning, offers future salmonid-ova experiments only when material available. P4 seventy-two-hour survival concerns a young charr barely covered with water, not ova exposed for seventy-two hours: editorial summary conflates these. P5 ova taken from trout stomach later hatched; P6 discusses moisture-preserved ova and only suspects partial drying fatal. Existing observations, proposed experiments and hypotheses remain distinct. Undated Darwin portfolio mark does not prove receipt January 30.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1651A: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 21, 1855 catalogue record with one bracketed editorial synopsis only. No authentic Davy letter or paper prose is transcribed. Record itself fully inspected, authentic body unavailable. Synopsis mentions January 28 enquiry, experimental conditions and intended Royal Society submission; it cannot be a training question. Subsequent Darwin acknowledgements identify a real paper, but do not supply its omitted wording. Differing 1856 publication references in nearby apparatus require version checking before any attempted recovery.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1653: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 25, supplied 1855. Arrived home late yesterday, March 24, and found Davy paper already there; its earlier physical delivery date is unstated. Pleased by epistolary form and plans to forward in two or three days. Has brought Angler and his Friend, but later April 25 reading record is not March completion. Documented reply to paper represented by synopsis-only 1651A, held as missing authentic prompt rather than fabricated Q/A.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1654: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 26, supplied 1855. Explicitly has just read Davy paper, reports interest in three-day moss exposure, moist-air survival, developmental-stage differences and temperature effects, requests possible replication and plans sending today. Do not infer that requested repetition happened; footnote finds no evidence. Royal Society March 27 receipt and April 26 reading are later external events. Bibliography lists a February 1856 reading under a differently described paper, requiring source-version care. Authentic incoming manuscript absent here, so no training pair with editorial synopsis.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
